name: Skills
lines: Felling trees for their logs: birch, oak, maple, yew and ironbark in the Guildlands, and timber, driftwood and fallen pines in every world.
Ore, coal, stone and gems: iron and coal, silver, gold, moonsilver and starstone at Hollowfell, and every vein, seam and crystal in every world.
Trout, pike, salmon, sea bass and swordfish in the Guildlands, and the fish, pearls and shells of every sea and lake.
Herbs, berries and mushrooms: thyme, sage, feverfew, moonpetal and starbloom, and every plant, moss and cap in every world.
Snares and tracking: rabbit, pheasant, deer, boar and elk for meat and hides, and feathers, scales and hides wherever they are found.
Weapons, armour and smelting at every forge, the Guild's bars of silver, gold, moonsilver and starstone, and the better axes and pickaxes.
Bows, staves, carts and brooms at every joinery, sawing logs into seasoned hardwood, and the better fishing rods.
Tanning leather, and the better forager's satchels and snare kits from leather, canvas and wire.
Cars, motorbikes, lorries, hovercars, war machines, firearms and machine parts at the Transport Yard and the Motor Pool.
Dishes from what you catch, snare and forage. Eating one fills your Food bar and makes you Well fed: you learn every craft faster for a while.
Draughts from herbs: more from every gather, steadier hands at the forge, keener eyes for rare finds, quicker learning.
Cutting gems, and rings and bracelets that raise the level of a craft while you hold them.

the Masters of each craft

Ottilie Hammerwright, the Toolmaker
Axes, picks, rods, satchels, snares. Iron, steel or darksteel. Better than that, you'll have to make yourself.

the Toolmaker of the Guild of Hands in Anvilmere: brisk, practical, proud of a good edge. She sells iron, steel and darksteel tools for woodcutting, mining, fishing, foraging and hunting, and explains that the Starmetal and Dreamforged tools are only made by members with materials that are only found.
The Toolmaker's counter
Guildmaster Hesper Vane
Welcome to the Guild of Hands. Twelve crafts, and a lifetime in each, if you want it.
The Guildmaster's table
The Smithy and Smelter
Master Brannock, the Guild smith
Bars at the smelter, tools at my anvil, blades and armour at the forge. Mind the sparks.

the Master Smith of the Guild of Hands in Anvilmere: a big, patient man who loves iron. He explains smelting silver, gold, moonsilver and starstone bars, making steel to Dreamforged axes and pickaxes, and that every Smithing level steadies a smith's hammer at any forge.
The Joinery and Sawpit
The Guild joinery bench
Master Elinor Ashgrove, the Guild joiner
Birch to ironbark, it all comes here. Better logs saw into more timber.

the Master Joiner of the Guild of Hands: quiet, precise, smells of sawdust. She explains sawing logs into seasoned hardwood (better logs give more), making steel to Dreamforged fishing rods, and bows, staves, carts and brooms at the joinery bench.
Mother Pell, the Guild cook
Hungry? Bring me a trout and I'll teach you to grill it. Bring me an elk and we'll talk about a feast.

the Master Cook of the Guild of Hands: round, loud, generous. She teaches dishes from what members catch, snare and forage (grilled trout, berry tart, roast pheasant with thyme, pike and mushroom pie, salmon with sage, venison stew, sea bass with thyme, boar roast with brambles, swordfish steak, the elk feast). A dish fills the Food bar and makes you Well fed, so you learn every craft faster.
Master Quillon Moss, the Guild apothecary
Thyme for plenty, sage for steady hands, feverfew for keen eyes, moonpetal for insight. And starbloom, for those who can find it.

the Master Apothecary of the Guild of Hands: thin, curious, ink-stained. He teaches draughts from herbs: Plenty (more from every gather), Steady Hands (a steadier hammer at the forge), Keen Eyes (rare finds twice as likely), Insight (quicker learning) and the Elixir of the Masters. Each needs a glass vial.
The Tanner's and Weaver's Hall
make satchels and snares
Master Wren Calloway, the Guild tanner
Leather for the satchel, wire for the snare. The good ones need something you have to find.

the Master Tanner and Weaver of the Guild of Hands: wiry, dry-humoured. She explains tanning hides into leather, and making steel to Dreamforged forager's satchels and snare kits from leather, canvas and wire.
cut gems and set rings
Master Aurelio Finch, the Guild jeweller
A cut garnet in a silver band, and the wearer cuts timber like a woodsman three years older.

the Master Jeweller of the Guild of Hands: soft-spoken, exact, loupe always in his eye. He cuts quartz, garnet, sapphire, emerald and ruby, and sets rings of silver, gold, moonsilver and starstone that raise a gathering craft's level while held, and the Artisan's bracelet for the making crafts.
Master Isambard Cole, the Guild engineer
Every Engineering level is a truer gear and a better weld. You'll feel it on the road.

the Master Engineer of the Guild of Hands: cheerful, oil to the elbows. He explains that Engineering is learned building cars, motorbikes, lorries, hovercars, war machines, firearms and machine parts at the Transport Yard, the Motor Pool or here, and every level makes the work finer.

The Forester's Lodge
Master Corwen Holt, the Forester
Birch near the road, oak past the first stream, maple where it turns red, then yew, then the ironbarks. Take what's marked.

the Master Forester of the Guild of Hands, keeper of the Greatwood north of Anvilmere: weathered, calm, fond of trees. The best trees grow deeper in: birch (level 1), oak (12), maple (24), yew (36), ironbark (48). The trees members may fell have a ribbon tied round them; a felled one grows back. Each needs an axe. Sometimes a Dreamheart burl is found in a good tree.
Master Dagny Flint, the Quarrymaster
Iron and coal on the top bench. Silver, gold, moonsilver down the benches. Starstone right at the bottom. Hard hats are a good idea.

the Quarrymaster of Hollowfell, the open quarry east of Anvilmere: blunt, safety-minded, proud. The pit has five benches: iron and coal (level 1), silver (12), gold (24), moonsilver (36) and starstone (48) at the bottom, and rough gems turn up in the rock. Each needs a pickaxe. Sometimes star crystal is found deep down.
Master Tobias Reed, the Water-bailiff
Trout in the river, pike in Mirrormere, salmon at the falls. Sea bass off the rocks and swordfish off the end of the long pier, if you've the arms for it.

the Water-bailiff of the Guild of Hands, at the boathouse on Mirrormere: patient, a teller of fish stories. Trout in the river (level 1), pike in Mirrormere (12), salmon at the falls to the north-west (24), sea bass off the rocks of the Saltreach coast (36), swordfish from the end of the long pier (48). Each needs a rod. A Moonpearl is a rare find.
The Herb Garden Shed
Mistress Marjory Thyme, the Herbwife
Thyme and brambles all over Thymewold. Sage and mushroom rings to the east. Feverfew on the slopes, moonpetal on the moor, starbloom at the top.

the Herbwife of the Guild of Hands, in Thymewold south of Anvilmere: kindly, sharp-eyed. Thyme and bramble berries in the meadows (level 1), wild sage and mushroom rings to the south-east (12), feverfew on the hillsides (24), moonpetal on the High Moor (36), starbloom on its tops (48). Each needs a forager's satchel. Dreamer's clover is a rare find.
Master Garrick Venn, the Huntsman
Warrens west of here, pheasants in the cover east of town, deer trails in the east woods, boar down by the marsh, and elk up on the far moor.

the Huntsman of the Guild of Hands: quiet, respectful of the animals, all snares and tracking, no needless cruelty. Rabbit warrens in the western meadows (level 1), pheasant cover between the town and the quarry (12), deer trails in the eastern woods (24), boar wallows by the marsh south of Mirrormere (36), elk on the far moor (48). Each needs a snare kit. A Silverwhite antler is a rare find.

The Guildlands. Anvilmere's square, the Guildhall before you: the Guildmaster and the Toolmaker are inside. The workshops stand round the square; the roads go out to the Greatwood (north), Hollowfell quarry (east), Mirrormere (west), the Saltreach and the long pier (south) and the High Moor (south-east). Safe everywhere.
